title: Payment Protection Schedule of Involuntary Unemployment Terms
content:
Involuntary unemployment of a covered person is a protected event on two Payment Protection plans, Payment Protection Complete and Joint Payment Protection Complete. On the four other plans each unemployment term reads "not covered".

## Unemployment terms by plan

| Plan | Job losses not covered within (days after enrollment) | Continuous full-time employment required before the job loss (months) | Elimination period (continuous days of unemployment before benefits begin) | Benefits paid from | Most monthly benefits per claim | Most monthly benefits over the plan's life |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Protection Life | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered |
| Payment Protection Life and Disability | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered |
| Payment Protection Complete | 90 | 6 | 30 | the first loan due date after the elimination period | 6 | 12 |
| Joint Payment Protection Life | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered |
| Joint Payment Protection Life and Disability | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered |
| Joint Payment Protection Complete | 90 | 6 | 30 | the first loan due date after the elimination period | 6 | 12 |

## Notes to the schedule

1. **Exclusion after enrollment.** Job losses within 90 days after enrollment are not covered on either plan.
2. **Prior employment.** The covered person needs 6 months of continuous full-time employment before the job loss.
3. **Start of payment.** An unemployment benefit is paid from the first loan due date after the 30-day elimination period of continuous unemployment.
4. **Month limits.** One unemployment claim receives at most 6 monthly benefits; the plan receives at most 12 monthly unemployment benefits over its life.
